From 1974 until 1988, Lantana hosted the tradition of displaying the world's largest decorated Christmas tree. Every year, a huge tree was shipped from the [Pacific Northwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Northwest "Pacific Northwest") to Lantana by rail to the grounds of the _[National Enquirer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Enquirer "National Enquirer")_, adjacent to the [Florida East Coast Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_East_Coast_Railway "Florida East Coast Railway") tracks. The event attracted many visitors each night and became one of the holiday events in South Florida. This ended in 1989 due to the sale of the _National Enquirer_ following the death of its founder, [Generoso Pope Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generoso_Pope_Jr. "Generoso Pope Jr."), at the age of 61 in October 1988.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-13)
In 2025, the Florida Supreme Court let stand more than $100,000 in fines the town levied on a homeowner for having allowed cars to be parked on her property with two tires occasionally resting on the lawn.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-15)
According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the town has a total area of 2.9 square miles (7.5 km 2), of which 0.6 sq mi (1.6 km 2) (21.31%) is covered by water.

Lantana has a [tropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_climate "Tropical climate"), more specifically a [tropical rainforest climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_rainforest_climate "Tropical rainforest climate") ([Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification")_Af_), as its driest month (February) averages 2.55 in (64.8 mm) of precipitation, meeting the minimum standard of 60 mm in the driest month needed to qualify for that designation.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-16) Much of the year is warm to hot in Lantana, and frost is extremely rare. As is typical in the Miami metropolitan area, two basic seasons occur in Lantana, a mild and dry winter (November through April), and a hot and wet summer (May through October). Daily thundershowers are common in the hot season, though they are brief. The town of Lantana is home to many varieties of [tropical vegetation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_vegetation "Tropical vegetation"), which can be seen in its variety of plants, trees, and flowers all over South Florida and the town itself, including its namesake, the [lantana flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana "Lantana").

Lantana is part of the [Miami metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_metropolitan_area "Miami metropolitan area") of South Florida.
As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Lantana had a population of 11,504. The median age was 43.3 years. 18.3% of residents were under the age of 18 and 19.4% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 95.2 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 93.1 males age 18 and over.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-20)
100.0% of residents lived in urban areas, while 0.0% lived in rural areas.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DHC-21)

There were 4,649 households in Lantana, of which 25.5% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 34.4% were married-couple households, 24.4% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 32.3% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 36.2% of all households were made up of individuals and 15.5% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-19)
There were 5,659 housing units, of which 17.8% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 2.6% and the rental vacancy rate was 16.8%.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-19)
As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), 2,556 families resided in the town.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-22)

As of the [2010 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census"), 10,423 people, 4,164 households, and 2,128 families were residing in the town.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-24)
In 2000, the age distribution included 6.1% under 5, 21.4% under 18, and 13.8% were 65 years or older. The median income for a household in the town was $41,624. About 17.4% of the population was below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line").
As of 2000, English as a first language accounted for 73.24% of all residents, and Spanish was found to be the first language of 13.95%, French Creole made up 6.82%, and Finnish was spoken by 5.01% of the population (the [highest percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finntown "Finntown") in Florida). Also, French was spoken by 0.62% of residents and German was spoken by 0.34% of the populace.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-25)
As of 2000, Lantana had the 111th-highest percentage of Finns in the US, which accounted for 5.4% of all residents (tied with two US areas in Michigan),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-26) and |Haitians had the 35th highest percentage, with 5.20% of the population.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-27)
Lantana was the publishing headquarters of the _[National Enquirer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Enquirer "National Enquirer")_ during the 1970s and much of the 1980s.

The Town of Lantana has a public library, with a collection of more than 24,000 volumes, as of 2020.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-29) The Lantana Road Library west of the city in unincorporated Palm Beach County is a branch of the public [Palm Beach County Library System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Beach_County_Library_System "Palm Beach County Library System").

From 1974 until 1988, Lantana hosted the tradition of displaying the world's largest decorated Christmas tree. Every year, a huge tree was shipped from the [Pacific Northwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Northwest "Pacific Northwest") to Lantana by rail to the grounds of the _[National Enquirer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Enquirer "National Enquirer")_, adjacent to the [Florida East Coast Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_East_Coast_Railway "Florida East Coast Railway") tracks. The event attracted many visitors each night and became one of the holiday events in South Florida. This ended in 1989 due to the sale of the _National Enquirer_ following the death of its founder, [Generoso Pope Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generoso_Pope_Jr. "Generoso Pope Jr."), at the age of 61 in October 1988.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-13)
In 2025, the Florida Supreme Court let stand more than $100,000 in fines the town levied on a homeowner for having allowed cars to be parked on her property with two tires occasionally resting on the lawn.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-15)
According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the town has a total area of 2.9 square miles (7.5 km 2), of which 0.6 sq mi (1.6 km 2) (21.31%) is covered by water.
texts.8: Lantana has a [tropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_climate "Tropical climate"), more specifically a [tropical rainforest climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_rainforest_climate "Tropical rainforest climate") ([Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification")_Af_), as its driest month (February) averages 2.55 in (64.8 mm) of precipitation, meeting the minimum standard of 60 mm in the driest month needed to qualify for that designation.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana,_Florida#cite_note-16) Much of the year is warm to hot in Lantana, and frost is extremely rare. As is typical in the Miami metropolitan area, two basic seasons occur in Lantana, a mild and dry winter (November through April), and a hot and wet summer (May through October). Daily thundershowers are common in the hot season, though they are brief. The town of Lantana is home to many varieties of [tropical vegetation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_vegetation "Tropical vegetation"), which can be seen in its variety of plants, trees, and flowers all over South Florida and the town itself, including its namesake, the [lantana flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantana "Lantana").

A variety of subject matter and different record types can be found among the holdings of the Still Picture Branch at the National Archives and Records Administration. Included in the holdings are topics such as African Art from the Harmon Foundation, images related to the Revolutionary War, and more. In addition to the traditional photographic prints and negatives within the Still Picture Branch holdings are series of posters, original artworks, and other record types. Listed below are selected lists of records related to various subject matter, as well as example series of different types of records.

## Posters
In addition to still photography, the Still Picture Branch also houses different graphic materials received from Federal Agencies as records. Over 50,000 posters are included in the Still Picture holdings. Many of the posters were created during the two World Wars and are found in the records of military organizations and civilian agencies supporting the war effort. The Still Picture Branch holdings also incorporate a large number of posters publicizing government peacetime and nonmilitary programs and subjects. Find more information about our holdings of World War II posters on our blog, ["We Can Do It!: World War II Posters at the Still Picture Branch."](https://unwritten-record.blogs.archives.gov/2020/09/22/we-can-do-it-world-war-ii-posters-at-the-still-picture-branch/)

## Posters
### Series of interest:
44-PA: **[World War II Posters, 1942 - 1945](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/513498)**
This series consists of posters created by various Federal Agencies to promote the war effort. The series is entirely digitized and available through our online catalog.
174-B: [**World War I-Era Broadsides, ca. 1940 - 2017**](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/99289923)
This series consists of broadsides that were issued by the Department of Labor under Secretary William Bauchop Wilson during and immediately after World War I. The series is digitized and available through our online catalog.
179-WP: **[War Production Board, 1942 - 1943](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/533858)** (Fully digitized)
This series consists of posters used in various production drives instituted by the War Production Board. This series is entirely digitized and available through our online catalog.

## Artwork
While many series within the holdings of the Still Picture Branch are photographs of artwork, there are also a few series of original artwork. The artwork ranges from cartoons to poster artwork to costume design, and more. Alternatively, the photographs of artwork include the United States Army Art Collection, images of stolen artwork and cultural objects, and more.

## Artwork
### Series of interest:
208-AOP: **[Original Artwork for World War II Posters, 1942 - 1945](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/2842724)**
This series consists of original artwork and a few photographs for World War II-era posters. The series is entirely digitized and available through our online catalog.
69-PIN: **[Sketches of Costumes for a Production of "Pinocchio", 1939 - 1939](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/518279)**
This series consists of watercolor and graphite sketches of costumes for a New York Federal Theater Project production of “Pinocchio.” The series is entirely digitized and available through our online catalog.
111-CCA:**[Color Contact Prints of the U.S. Army Art Collection, 1958 - 1981](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/530639)**
This series consists of photographs of artworks that document a wide variety of subjects from World War I, World War II, the Korean War and the Vietnam War. This series is not entirely digitized, however, it is available for request in the Still Picture Research Room.

## Select Lists of Photographs
These lists of photographs highlight various records related to a specific topic or subject. The records included in these lists only cover a portion of the holdings of the Still Picture Branch. The majority of the photographs within the holdings of the Still Picture Branch have not been digitized on our online catalog.
[**Contemporary African Art, Harmon Foundation**](https://www.archives.gov/research/african-art)
This select list of images consists of photographs of artwork related to the Harmon Foundation’s collections of Contemporary African Art. The list includes photographs of artwork by select artists within our holdings.
[**Images of the Revolutionary War**](https://www.archives.gov/research/military/american-revolution/pictures)
This select list of images consists of copies of artwork related to the American Revolutionary War. Events include the Prelude to War, War at Sea, portraits of notable people, and more.

## To Request Information about Records
For further information about the photographs and graphic works held in the [Still Picture unit at College Park](https://www.archives.gov/research/still-pictures/visit), contact:

texts.0: A variety of subject matter and different record types can be found among the holdings of the Still Picture Branch at the National Archives and Records Administration. Included in the holdings are topics such as African Art from the Harmon Foundation, images related to the Revolutionary War, and more. In addition to the traditional photographic prints and negatives within the Still Picture Branch holdings are series of posters, original artworks, and other record types. Listed below are selected lists of records related to various subject matter, as well as example series of different types of records.
texts.1:
## Posters
In addition to still photography, the Still Picture Branch also houses different graphic materials received from Federal Agencies as records. Over 50,000 posters are included in the Still Picture holdings. Many of the posters were created during the two World Wars and are found in the records of military organizations and civilian agencies supporting the war effort. The Still Picture Branch holdings also incorporate a large number of posters publicizing government peacetime and nonmilitary programs and subjects. Find more information about our holdings of World War II posters on our blog, ["We Can Do It!: World War II Posters at the Still Picture Branch."](https://unwritten-record.blogs.archives.gov/2020/09/22/we-can-do-it-world-war-ii-posters-at-the-still-picture-branch/)
texts.2:
## Posters
### Series of interest:
44-PA: **[World War II Posters, 1942 - 1945](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/513498)**
This series consists of posters created by various Federal Agencies to promote the war effort. The series is entirely digitized and available through our online catalog.
174-B: [**World War I-Era Broadsides, ca. 1940 - 2017**](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/99289923)
This series consists of broadsides that were issued by the Department of Labor under Secretary William Bauchop Wilson during and immediately after World War I. The series is digitized and available through our online catalog.
179-WP: **[War Production Board, 1942 - 1943](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/533858)** (Fully digitized)
This series consists of posters used in various production drives instituted by the War Production Board. This series is entirely digitized and available through our online catalog.
texts.3:
## Artwork
While many series within the holdings of the Still Picture Branch are photographs of artwork, there are also a few series of original artwork. The artwork ranges from cartoons to poster artwork to costume design, and more. Alternatively, the photographs of artwork include the United States Army Art Collection, images of stolen artwork and cultural objects, and more.
texts.4:
## Artwork
### Series of interest:
208-AOP: **[Original Artwork for World War II Posters, 1942 - 1945](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/2842724)**
This series consists of original artwork and a few photographs for World War II-era posters. The series is entirely digitized and available through our online catalog.
69-PIN: **[Sketches of Costumes for a Production of "Pinocchio", 1939 - 1939](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/518279)**
This series consists of watercolor and graphite sketches of costumes for a New York Federal Theater Project production of “Pinocchio.” The series is entirely digitized and available through our online catalog.
111-CCA:**[Color Contact Prints of the U.S. Army Art Collection, 1958 - 1981](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/530639)**
This series consists of photographs of artworks that document a wide variety of subjects from World War I, World War II, the Korean War and the Vietnam War. This series is not entirely digitized, however, it is available for request in the Still Picture Research Room.
texts.5:
## Select Lists of Photographs
These lists of photographs highlight various records related to a specific topic or subject. The records included in these lists only cover a portion of the holdings of the Still Picture Branch. The majority of the photographs within the holdings of the Still Picture Branch have not been digitized on our online catalog.
[**Contemporary African Art, Harmon Foundation**](https://www.archives.gov/research/african-art)
This select list of images consists of photographs of artwork related to the Harmon Foundation’s collections of Contemporary African Art. The list includes photographs of artwork by select artists within our holdings.
[**Images of the Revolutionary War**](https://www.archives.gov/research/military/american-revolution/pictures)
This select list of images consists of copies of artwork related to the American Revolutionary War. Events include the Prelude to War, War at Sea, portraits of notable people, and more.

## Results
#### Display options
42.   [1970s-2021 ### Jack Goldstein films and papers The collection documents the artistic practice and estate administration of conceptual artist Jack Goldstein. It consists primarily of 16mm film materials related to Goldstein’s cinematic work, including titles such as _The Jump_ (1978), _Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer_ (1975), and _Shane_ (1975). Also included are photographs and slides of Goldstein’s visual works; a small selection of personal and professional papers; his text-based works _Selected Writings 1994-2000_, _Untitled (Selectric Works)_ (1988), and _Totems: Selected Writings_ (1988-1990); and his conceptual music recording _The Planets_ (1984). A portion of the collection comprises administrative materials from the Jack Goldstein Estate, which document the posthumous management and exhibition of his work by estate executor Rebecca Donelson. ### Creator: Goldstein, Jack, 1945-2003 Contains digital material](https://www.getty.edu/research/collections/collection/24Z686 "Jack Goldstein films and papers")

Correspondence, articles, black-and-white and color photographs, and a variety of printed ephemera record Joseph's role as the central communication point in a network of her father's colleagues, friends, and a generation of architectural historians. # City Archives
by [Anissa Di Vincente](https://www.culvercityhistoricalsociety.org/author/anissacchsadmin/)
The Historical Society archive acts as a satellite repository for City Hall records.
Included are documents from the offices of city council members and other officials.
The Parks and Recreation Dept. under the direction of Syd Kronenthal for more than 50 years, maintained complete records of programs, offerings, events and activities in huge scrapbooks which are available in the archive.
The history of La Ballona Fiesta since 1948 is documented through the years.
The Olympics of 1932 and 1984.
The historical record of various civic groups such as Chamber of Commerce, Optimists, Soroptimists, Lions Club and Woman’s Club are also represented here.
**Records Include**
*   Culver City Sister City – Early Collection  
*   Culver City Chamber of Commerce: 1920-1990’s  
*   Culver City Newpaper Collection  
*   Evening Star News: 1925-1947  
*   Citizen Newspapers  
*   Microfilm: 1940’s-1980’s

*   Sandford Bodger Collection: 1964-1982  
*   Culver City Maps: 1920 streets / Annexation map

# City Archives
by [Anissa Di Vincente](https://www.culvercityhistoricalsociety.org/author/anissacchsadmin/)
The Historical Society archive acts as a satellite repository for City Hall records.
Included are documents from the offices of city council members and other officials.
The Parks and Recreation Dept. under the direction of Syd Kronenthal for more than 50 years, maintained complete records of programs, offerings, events and activities in huge scrapbooks which are available in the archive.
The history of La Ballona Fiesta since 1948 is documented through the years.
The Olympics of 1932 and 1984.
The historical record of various civic groups such as Chamber of Commerce, Optimists, Soroptimists, Lions Club and Woman’s Club are also represented here.
**Records Include**
*   Culver City Sister City – Early Collection  
*   Culver City Chamber of Commerce: 1920-1990’s  
*   Culver City Newpaper Collection  
*   Evening Star News: 1925-1947  
*   Citizen Newspapers  
*   Microfilm: 1940’s-1980’s  
*   Culver City Woman’s Club: 1920’s-1940’s  
*   Culver City Unified School District  
*   Sandford Bodger Collection: 1964-1982  
*   Culver City Maps: 1920 streets / Annexation map  
*   Pacific Electric / Time Warner – Shay Hotel Dig  
*   Fox Hills Country Club/Symantec Dig

# City Archives
by [Anissa Di Vincente](https://www.culvercityhistoricalsociety.org/author/anissacchsadmin/)
The Historical Society archive acts as a satellite repository for City Hall records.
Included are documents from the offices of city council members and other officials.
The Parks and Recreation Dept. under the direction of Syd Kronenthal for more than 50 years, maintained complete records of programs, offerings, events and activities in huge scrapbooks which are available in the archive.
The history of La Ballona Fiesta since 1948 is documented through the years.
The Olympics of 1932 and 1984.
The historical record of various civic groups such as Chamber of Commerce, Optimists, Soroptimists, Lions Club and Woman’s Club are also represented here.
**Records Include**
*   Culver City Sister City – Early Collection  
*   Culver City Chamber of Commerce: 1920-1990’s  
*   Culver City Newpaper Collection  
*   Evening Star News: 1925-1947  
*   Citizen Newspapers  
*   Microfilm: 1940’s-1980’s  
*   Culver City Woman’s Club: 1920’s-1940’s  
*   Culver City Unified School District  
*   Sandford Bodger Collection: 1964-1982  
*   Culver City Maps: 1920 streets / Annexation map  
*   Pacific Electric / Time Warner – Shay Hotel Dig  
*   Fox Hills Country Club/Symantec Dig

# City Archives
by [Anissa Di Vincente](https://www.culvercityhistoricalsociety.org/author/anissacchsadmin/)
The Historical Society archive acts as a satellite repository for City Hall records.
Included are documents from the offices of city council members and other officials.
The Parks and Recreation Dept. under the direction of Syd Kronenthal for more than 50 years, maintained complete records of programs, offerings, events and activities in huge scrapbooks which are available in the archive.
The history of La Ballona Fiesta since 1948 is documented through the years.
The Olympics of 1932 and 1984.
The historical record of various civic groups such as Chamber of Commerce, Optimists, Soroptimists, Lions Club and Woman’s Club are also represented here.
**Records Include**
*   Culver City Sister City – Early Collection  
*   Culver City Chamber of Commerce: 1920-1990’s  
*   Culver City Newpaper Collection  
*   Evening Star News: 1925-1947  
*   Citizen Newspapers  
*   Microfilm: 1940’s-1980’s  
*   Culver City Woman’s Club: 1920’s-1940’s  
*   Culver City Unified School District  
*   Sandford Bodger Collection: 1964-1982  
*   Culver City Maps: 1920 streets / Annexation map  
*   Pacific Electric / Time Warner – Shay Hotel Dig  
*   Fox Hills Country Club/Symantec Dig
